title: Effort to restrict open-weight AI just hit a wall, industry and APEC back open source - TCR 07/25/26
description:
Hugging Face, Meta, Microsoft, Mistral, and Nvidia signed an open letter against restricting open AI weights the same week 21 APEC economies endorsed open-source cooperation in Chengdu, Anthropic shipped Opus 5 at roughly half of Fable's price, and Moody's warned AI capex is eroding the credit quality of six hyperscalers whose debt now competes with Treasurys.

https://sharedsapience.com/the-century-report-july-25-2026/

0:00 Open and framing
0:35 Industry opposes open-weight limits as APEC backs secure open-source AI
7:34 Anthropic ships Opus 5 at half of Fable's price
10:38 Moody's warns AI capex erodes hyperscaler credit
15:05 Solar outproduces coal and wind on the US grid
18:39 PRIMA implant wins EU clearance for reading vision
22:23 Close

This episode covers the industry coalition and APEC defense of open-weight AI, the collapse of the Kimi K3 distillation-theft claim, Anthropic's Opus 5 and its fourth-in-a-quarter price compression, Moody's hyperscaler credit warning and Alphabet's $811 billion in future spending commitments, solar outproducing coal and wind on the US grid in May, and the PRIMA retinal implant winning EU clearance.

The day's signal sits on one fault line: capability that stays public versus capability you have to rent. An industry coalition opposed broad open-weight restrictions in the same week 21 APEC economies backed open-source AI with strong security assurances, while researchers dismantled the distillation-theft claim used to justify locking it down, noting the model said to be stolen had only been public for weeks. Anthropic's Opus 5, its fourth 5-series release in two months, undercut its own flagship on price, showing frontier intelligence compressing toward commodity economics on a cadence measured in weeks. Underneath the governance fight, Moody's flagged that hyperscaler borrowing is eroding six giants' credit quality and helping hold 30-year yields above 5%. And the generative signal held: solar became the third-largest US power source in May, and PRIMA crossed from trial data into reimbursable sight across 30 countries.
